newsitem.title: USA: Chateau spurns Zell, Sun offers, for revised ROC deal.
newsitem.headline: Chateau spurns Zell, Sun offers, for revised ROC deal.

text.p: Chateau Properties Inc. Wednesday spurned two takeover offers from rival mobile home park operators in favour of a revised merger deal with its original partner ROC Communities Inc.

Since Chateau signed a merger agreement with ROC in July, Sun Communities Inc. and Chicago developer Samuel Zell's Manufactured Home Communities Inc. have approached the real estate investment trust with their own offers.

Chateau said it rejected Manufactured Home's $400 million, $26-a-share, offer as inadequate and said the long-term benefits of a combination with ROC were superior to a merger with Sun, which offered $390 million.
"We are just getting the details," Zell said. "But I would highly doubt it puts an end to our offer."
Chateau and ROC maintain that their "merger of equals" agreement reached in July would benefit common shareholders.
"It is a long-term strategic business combination that we are convinced is going to be in the long-term interest of shareholders," ROC Chief Executive Gary McDaniel said.
He and Chateau Chief Executive Jeff Kellogg said in an interview the companies' properties and management teams merge well, and the executives expect growth in the new company. Under the revised RROC
deal, Chateau shareholders would receive a greater amount of stock per Chateau share in the new company.

Clinton Township, Mich.-based Chateau also said it planned to buy back up to 1.45 million of its common shares, about 24 percent of its outstanding stock. ROC said it would purchase as many as 350,000 Chateau shares before the merger.
The amended deal also lowered the Chateau votes needed to approve the merger to a simple majority of shares rather than two-thirds.

The combined company will be renamed Chateau Communities Inc. and will be based at ROC's current offices in Englewood, Colo. The legal structure of the merger will be modified so that ROC will merge into a newly-formed subsidiary of Chateau.

Under the revised deal, each Chateau common share will be exchanged for 1.0316 shares of the combined entity, rather than one share as originally planned. The exchange ratio for ROC stockholders was unchanged at 1.042.

Besides Chateau's shareholders, who vote and elect a board of directors, the company also has operating partnership unit holders, who do not vote and are mostly the directors and managers of the real estate investment trust.
Also included in the new deal was an option for Chateau's unit holders to swap units for common shares, enabling them to defer what would be significant capital gains taxes.
There are more units than Chateau shares, and the effective exchange ratio could increase if holders of those units opt to convert them into common stock.

Chateau said it filed a lawsuit against Manufactured Home on Tuesday, alleging that the company's bid violated federal securities laws, that Manufactured Home began a proxy solicitation to foil Chateau's merger with ROC by making material misstatements of facts and failing to disclose other material facts.
The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland.

Chateau said it also faces a class-action lawsuit filed Sept. 12 alleging that its directors violated their fiduciary duties to stockholders by agreeing to the merger with ROC and refusing to endorse the Manufactured Home offer.
Chateau's stock fell $1.75 to $24.875 and ROC slid 37.5 cents to $23.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
